terminal.emulator: direct PTY with deterministic loopback HTTP/SSE tool-call fixture

reference.capture: fresh synthetic-home Hermes TUI process with one ordinary prompt; the loopback provider requests one terminal tool call whose only side effect writes a probe-owned sandbox file; the follow-up tool result is answered with a plain completion; bounded post-completion observation window

normalization: The reference checkout, synthetic HOME/HERMES_HOME paths, prompt text, assistant text, tool arguments, credentials, authorization values, session identifiers, timestamps, and redraw bytes are omitted or represented by stable markers or digests.

The provider is a deterministic 127.0.0.1 fixture owned by the probe; all recorded HTTP traffic stayed on that loopback endpoint and no external network, OAuth flow, browser, or user credential was used.

The executed command is a synthetic probe-owned command whose only side effect writes into the probe sandbox (mkdir -p <sandbox>/out && echo synthetic > <sandbox>/out/out.txt); the command's structure is recorded as markers (contains mkdir/echo/redirection/chaining and the expected basename) and the arguments as length/digest, never the raw command text or sandbox path. The argument digest embeds the probe-owned path and therefore varies per run.

The real Hermes terminal tool-result content is recorded only as normalized shape (content kind, length, digest, JSON top-level keys, boolean anchors); the content itself is never persisted. The 45-byte result digest was identical across three fresh runs (708054e2...), including runs with different sandbox paths.
The [DONE] marker completes the tool-call stream so tool processing and execution proceed; the sandbox and HOME/HERMES_HOME are removed after the probe.

steps.precondition: Fresh Hermes TUI at 120x40 with an isolated synthetic HERMES_HOME and a configured custom provider at the probe-owned loopback endpoint.

side_effect_boundary.external_network: none observed; all recorded HTTP traffic stayed on the synthetic loopback
side_effect_boundary.credentials: none; only a synthetic key was placed in the throwaway config and auth values were reduced to presence booleans
side_effect_boundary.filesystem: tool side effects were confined to the probe-owned sandbox directory under a throwaway temp root; the sandbox was removed after the probe
side_effect_boundary.tool_action: one terminal command whose only side effect writes the probe-owned sandbox file (mkdir -p <sandbox>/out && echo synthetic > <sandbox>/out/out.txt)

unknowns: Approval UI, retry, failure-path, and timing semantics for the terminal tool remain unknown beyond this single fresh observation; the observed command matched no dangerous pattern and executed without an approval prompt.

Whether the terminal tool result content (output text, exit code, error field, cwd, duration fields) is stable across reference restarts remains bounded by this single observation; the 45-byte result digest was stable across three runs with different sandbox paths.
The processing-marker visibility is timing-dependent (observed in the canonical run, absent in an earlier run) and is not asserted by the probe.
The purpose of the auxiliary non-stream system/user request seen in OBS-0108/0109/0114/0116/0119 remains unclassified and is not a Hades requirement.
